nodes.label: MEMORY & SECOND BRAIN
nodes.detail: The core. Where knowledge is stored, structured, and survives between sessions.

nodes.label: advanced-claude-md
nodes.detail: Advanced CLAUDE.md and system prompt optimization — structure, imports, rules hierarchy, and quality improvement patterns from the Claude Code Advanced Course.

nodes.label: hermes-learn
nodes.detail: Teach Claude (or Hermes Agent) a new workflow from any source — URL, PDF, doc, code folder, or pasted notes — and save it as a reusable skill.md that auto-loads in future sessions.

nodes.label: obsidian-memory
nodes.detail: Persistent memory layer using Obsidian + NotebookLM MCP — store, retrieve, and cross-reference knowledge across AI sessions so context is never lost between conversations.

nodes.label: skill-generator
nodes.detail: Meta-skill — generate a new .claude/skills/ entry from any pasted video description, article, or doc. Extracts tool names, URLs, chapter structure, and key concepts, then writes the SKILL.md, adds README entries, commits, and pushes. Formalizes the hermes-learn pattern.
sections: When one video produces multiple skills

nodes.label: workspace-org
nodes.detail: Workspace organization for personal, business, and client projects in Claude Code — session naming, worktrees, project separation, and context hygiene.

nodes.label: JARVIS INTERFACE
nodes.detail: How you talk to the brain — voice, dashboards, and the daily briefing.

nodes.label: agent-os
nodes.detail: Agentic OS — the full Agent Operating System running at localhost:3737/hermes. Covers the sidebar layout, agent roster, orchestration tools, and navigation tabs inside the Hermes web UI.

nodes.label: hermes-jarvis
nodes.detail: Hermes-Jarvis voice interface — the orb UI inside localhost:3737/hermes. Covers Neural Link controls (Realtime, Live, Wake word, Auto mode, Briefing, Ash persona) and how to interact.
sections: Speed fixes if Jarvis feels slow

nodes.label: morning-brief
nodes.detail: Automated morning brief — aggregates news, calendar, tasks, emails, and market data into a single daily summary delivered via your preferred channel (voice, Slack, email, or Telegram).

nodes.label: wispr-flow
nodes.detail: Wispr Flow — system-wide voice-to-text for Mac. Dictate into any app including Claude Code, terminals, and chat interfaces. Covers setup, dictation patterns, and voice prompting for agentic workflows.
sections: Why it matters for agentic work

nodes.label: AGENT ENGINE
nodes.detail: The automation muscle — orchestration, parallelism, safety rails.

nodes.label: agent-harness
nodes.detail: Build larger projects using agent harnesses — orchestrator + worker patterns, task queues, and structured handoffs between Claude instances.

nodes.label: agent-teams
nodes.detail: Parallelization techniques — agent teams, stochastic consensus, debate patterns, and multi-agent problem solving with Claude Code.

nodes.label: agentic-harness
nodes.detail: Agentic harness engineering — the model is the brain (rented), the harness is the body (owned). Covers the agent loop, harness anatomy, content forge pattern, voice-reviewer agent, handoff prompts, and the build-with-frontier/execute-with-open-source strategy.
sections: Build with frontier, execute with open source
Getting started: steal a good one

nodes.label: always-on-agents
nodes.detail: Always-on agentic OS — running 3 AI agents 24/7 for 30 days. Covers the complete stack: CLAUDE.md for persistent memory, MCP for tool connections, and a setup you can build in under 30 minutes.
sections: What 30 days of running 3 agents taught

nodes.label: autoresearch
nodes.detail: Karpathy-style auto-research loop — Claude autonomously researches a topic, generates hypotheses, tests them, and iteratively improves its own knowledge base.

nodes.label: browser-automation
nodes.detail: Browser automation with Claude Code — choosing between Playwright, Browser Use, Computer Use, and browser-cdp based on the task type.

nodes.label: claude-managed-agents
nodes.detail: Claude Managed Agents — Anthropic-hosted agent runtime. Covers the three core concepts (agent/environment/session), production checklist, four build steps, secrets management, scheduling, and cost breakdown.
sections: Why most AI agents fail (the two reasons)
Four steps to build an agent
How to actually use it today

nodes.label: claude-security
nodes.detail: Security practices for Claude Code projects — auto-mode classifier, OAuth, permission scoping, secrets management, and protecting against prompt injection.

nodes.label: human-validation
nodes.detail: Human-validation zones — structured checkpoints in agentic workflows where a human must review before the AI continues. The pattern that makes autonomous agents safe to run on real work.
sections: The problem with fully autonomous agents
Zone placement in a real workflow

nodes.label: n8n-vs-mcp
nodes.detail: n8n vs MCP decision guide — when to use visual workflow automation (n8n) vs native AI tool connections (MCP), and how Claude/Hermes fit as no-code workflow builders.

nodes.label: paperclip-teams
nodes.detail: Paperclip-orchestrated agent teams — run a lead orchestrator that coordinates multiple specialized sub-agents using local or free Claude Code instances for complex multi-step work.
sections: Automated image + blog SEO workflow (community build)

nodes.label: BUSINESS LAUNCHPAD
nodes.detail: Turning the brain into revenue — the LLC, client sites, and service lines.

nodes.label: buildpartner
nodes.detail: BuildPartner — AI-accelerated product development tool built on Claude Code. Covers the 10x speed methodology, how it pairs with Claude Code, and when to use it vs. building directly with the CLI.
sections: The 10x speed claim (where it actually comes from)
How it pairs with Claude Code

nodes.label: claude-cms
nodes.detail: Build a client-handoff website with a built-in CMS using Claude Code — blueprint extractor, one-shot build, safety layer, MongoDB Atlas backend, Vercel deployment. Clients edit their own site without touching code or touching you.

nodes.label: claude-freelance
nodes.detail: Sell Claude Code builds as a $5,000 local business service — the pricing model, client pitch, WordPress workflow, and agency economics. Build in 2 hours what used to take 2 weeks.
sections: The economics of local business SEO sites
What to say to close the deal

nodes.label: claude-seo
nodes.detail: Claude SEO — 12 open-source Claude Code skills that replace a $5–10K/month SEO agency stack. Covers parallel SEO audits, health scores, PDF reports, schema markup, GEO (AI search optimization), sitemap, hreflang, and competitor analysis. One install command.

nodes.label: ghl-automation
nodes.detail: Automate GoHighLevel with Claude Code via the GHL CLI — build triggers, conditions, and email sequences in plain English without ever opening the GHL dashboard. Full workflow automation through prompts.
sections: What Claude can build for you

nodes.label: hermes-oracle
nodes.detail: Hermes Oracle — one-click SEO blog post publishing. Pulls trending news from Twitter/X, generates SEO-optimized content, and publishes to WordPress automatically.

nodes.label: lovable-ai
nodes.detail: Lovable AI — prompt-to-app builder. Describe a web app in plain English, get a working full-stack app deployed in minutes. Covers the build loop, tech stack, GitHub sync, and when to use Lovable vs Claude Code.
sections: When to use Lovable vs Claude Code

nodes.label: premium-website
nodes.detail: Build a $10,000-quality website with Claude Code — the 8-pillar checklist, design skills setup, reference-based prompting, imagery, polish passes, and live deployment. No coding, no templates, no generic AI look.

nodes.label: vibe-coding
nodes.detail: Vibe Coding Incubator — AI-first developer training. Build real apps with LLMs, prompting patterns, and agentic workflows from idea to deployed product. Covers the core methodology and how it pairs with Claude Code.
sections: The three skills vibe coding trains
How it pairs with Claude Code
Common anti-patterns (what the incubator teaches you to avoid)
